newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SAS backs Asian freighter despite profit problem.
newsitem.headline: SAS backs Asian freighter despite profit problem.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System remains committed to its Asian freighter service to Osaka in Japan via Macau after a first year of unprofitable operation, the airline's cargo sales director, Jan Hagen told Reuters.
But he raised doubts about the airline's long term loyalty to Macau after Hong Kong's new airport opens next year.
SAS began its Boeing 747 freighter service from Gothenburg to Osaka via Delhi and Macau as an alternative to slot restricted Kai Tak last April.

For the Portuguese enclave's new airport, attracting the European cargo carrier was seen by industry observers as a coup and the catalyst for other cargo carriers such as Asiana Airlines. SAS also pioneered using barges to transport cargo from Hong Kong to lower cost Macau airport.
When asked if SAS is making a profit with its first Asian freighter Hagen said: "Unfortunately not" but emphasised the carrier remains committed to the service as a whole.
"Rate levels have been sliding in the wrong direction and if we are going to make a zero result this year (break even) we shall be very lucky," Hagen added in a telephone interview.

SAS recently announced a 31 percent drop in profits blaming a combination of higher costs, currency movements and increasing competition. Hagen admitted he was under "extreme pressure" to make a profit. In order to break even and because of low yields, he said SAS must achieve 90 percent load factor on the Asian freighter service "which is extremely high."

When asked if that was achievable, Hagen said: "It is going to be tough. We know we can fill the flight from Macau and into Europe but we need to fill it both ways in order to achieve that. We are optimistic."

Hagen said changes have been made to try and ensure profitability. Delhi has been dropped and now the twice weekly freighter stops in Sharjah in the United Arab Emirates. Traffic rights have also been obtained so cargo can be flown into Macau from Europe.
"Especially with the midweek flight when we were not able to fill it with cargo bound for Osaka, it has given us the opportunity to load European exports for Macau and Hong Kong," Hagen added.
Hagen said SAS would be considering flying into Hong Kong's new airport at Chek Lap Kok due to open next year despite its higher cost structure.

"I think it would be natural for us to consider whether we should continue to fly into Macau or Hong Kong. One of the advantages of flying into Macau is that you are able to serve many parts of south China but when we talk about exports from Europe and into Macau, the final destination is Hong Kong," he said
But you could say that if we see lots of imports to south China, Macau could be the destination to continuously use," Hagen added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
